issue.title: MTProxy with fake-TLS secret (`ee…`) never connects: timestamp byte order in ClientHello + Abridged codec

comments.body:
Thanks for 2542ff9. I built `main` (b3caf01) from source and tested it against the same real fake-TLS proxy.

**Fixed:** the little-endian timestamp and the padded intermediate codec both work. With an existing session, regular requests (dialogs, history, search) go through the proxy fine.

**Still failing:** anything that creates a new auth key fails with `Error: Invalid unencrypted MTProto payload length`: first login with an empty `StringSession` (3 of 3 attempts) and media downloads that open a new sender (`downloadMedia` on a photo).

The cause is this check in `PaddedIntermediatePacketCodec.readPacket` for unencrypted packets:

```ts
const end = 20 + body.readUInt32LE(16);
if (end > length || length - end > 15) {
    throw new Error("Invalid unencrypted MTProto payload length");
}
```

The proxy pads unencrypted packets with far more than 15 bytes. Values I logged during the DH exchange (packet length / inner length field / trailing padding):

| length | field | padding |
|---|---|---|
| 172 | 80 | 72 |
| 166 | 80 | 66 |
| 759 | 632 | 107 |
| 73 | 52 | 1 |

So the `length - end > 15` bound rejects valid server packets. Relaxing the condition to just `if (end > length)` makes everything work on this proxy: fresh login, all requests, and photo downloads. The inner length field already tells where the payload ends, so the padding size does not need an upper bound here.
